neighbours.label: a certainty or evidential cue (certainly, definitely, surely, would suggest) and the predicate it asserts, as against the same predicate stated plainly
fire: Whatever the critics say, the new album certainly sounds better than the last one.
Looking at the photos, the house definitely looks older than they claimed.
The early results would seem to show that the drug works.
From what I saw, the twins certainly behave like rivals.
Reading her letters, one can surely see how lonely she was.
The rise in prices would suggest that demand is still strong.
Back then, the old mill certainly was the heart of the village.
In hindsight, his choice definitely proved to be the right one.
quiet: Whatever the critics say, the new album sounds louder than the last one.
Looking at the photos, the house looks older than the barn.
The early results show that the drug was given twice a day.
From what I saw, the twins behave like any other kids.
Reading her letters, one can learn how she spent her days.
The rise in prices began in the spring of last year.
Back then, the old mill was built from local stone.
In hindsight, his choice proved to be costly.

notes: Probe weak: 'certainly fit' 0.14, 'definitely' 0.12, 'would suggest' 0.26, plain 0.004. Output promotes 'surely', 'definitely', 'certainly'.
